# A function's local named like state of the component a test takes: a test
# build roots at `page`, whose `label` prop is a var of what it builds, and
# labelOf's own `var label` read as that var -- `m.label` on the Go targets,
# `state.label` on html and android -- since each emitter bound a function's
# parameters as locals and not what its body declares (codegen.BodyLocals).

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

struct Tag {
    label string
}

// Reads a local named like the page's prop, narrowed.
func labelOf(tags list[option[Tag]]) string {
    var out list[string] = []
    for var t = tags {
        var label = t
        if label != null {
            out.push(label.label)
        }
    }
    return out.format(",")
}

component page(label = "") ui.node {
    ui.text #shown(value=labelOf([Tag{label="a"}, null, Tag{label="b"}]) + label)
}

func testTheLocalIsItsOwn(t test.Test, c page) {
    t.assert(c.shown.value == "a,b")
}

ui.window {
    page()
}
